title: A finitely generated prime is associated exactly when it is weakly associated
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and M an R-module [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Let p be a prime ideal of R that is finitely generated. Say that p is associated to M when p is the annihilator of some element of M, and weakly associated to M when p is minimal among the prime ideals containing the annihilator of some element of M. Then p is associated to M if and only if p is weakly associated to M.

proof.text: If p is the annihilator of an element m of M, then p is itself a prime ideal containing Ann(m), so it is minimal among the prime ideals containing Ann(m). Thus associated implies weakly associated.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 10.66.9, tag 058A, proof (the reverse implication is immediate from the definitions)

proof.text: Assume p is weakly associated to M. By [lem-sc-weakass-localization], the localized module M_p contains an element m whose annihilator I has radical p R_p.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 10.66.2, tag 0566, applied in the proof of Lemma 10.66.9

proof.text: Write p = (g_1, ..., g_n). For each i, radical(I) = p R_p gives a least positive exponent e_i with g_i^{e_i} m = 0. Among all elements of M_p whose annihilator has radical p R_p, choose one for which the sum of these least exponents is minimal. If some e_i > 1, then m' = g_i^{e_i-1}m is nonzero by minimality of e_i. Every generator g_j has a power killing m', so p R_p is contained in radical(Ann(m')). Since m' is nonzero, Ann(m') is proper; because p R_p is the maximal ideal of R_p, this forces radical(Ann(m')) = p R_p. Thus m' is another admissible element with smaller exponent sum, a contradiction. Hence every e_i is 1, so p R_p is contained in Ann(m). Conversely Ann(m) is contained in radical(Ann(m)) = p R_p. Therefore Ann(m) = p R_p.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 10.66.9, tag 058A, proof (finite-generator exponent descent), with the maximal-ideal property of R_p from the localization definition

proof.text: The maximal ideal of R_p is now the annihilator of an element of M_p. Since p is finitely generated, [lem-sc-associated-localization-fg] descends this associated prime from the localization and yields an element of M whose annihilator is p. Thus p is associated to M.
